minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 13, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:01 p.m., on March 13, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 9, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:02 p.m.)
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation (Paragraph (1) of subdivision
  (d) of Section 54956.9): City of Mission Viejo v. State of California, DOF.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel: Initiation of Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (4) of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: 1 case.

City Council Minutes  1  March 13, 2018
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03, Mayor Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council provided direction to staff for item CS1. For
item CS2, the Council unanimously directed staff to pursue joinder of an Amicus Brief to support
the Federal Government’s action to turn back the Sanctuary State/City laws. Staff will be
evaluating that and the City Council will take final action in the future.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following expressed opposition to the change in hours and shifts for the Orange County Fire
Authority 911 Operators: Patsy DePalma, M.V.; Jon Dumitru, Orange; Chad Kurthy, Rancho
Santa Margarita; and Cody Quirarte, Lake Forest.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated that the speaker podium belongs to the public; it is where they come
to express concerns. She said that the Mayor was disrespectful to speakers during the last meeting
and the Council should be welcoming, not threatening.

The following expressed concern with the potential extension of the 241 Toll Road through San
Clemente: Michelle Sinning, M.V.; Elizabeth C., San Clemente; and Steven Viele, San Clemente.

Linda Cooper, M.V.: expressed concern with a home that sits empty on Alicante and has thick
weeds, lumber and trash on site. She asked if the City can do something about it.

Shayan Feiz, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the Community of Character Committee, he discussed
this month’s character word, “integrity,” and described attributes of that trait.

Martha Casey, M.V.: said that a sober living facility is opening on Via San Fernando and she asked
if the neighbors have any recourse if there are more than six residents. She also asked what
neighbors can do about nuisance factors such as parking issues, smoking, etc.

Michael Rotcher, M.V.: announced an upcoming conference called “Understanding Community
Choice Energy and Its Opportunities” which will be held on April 11, 2018, from 10:00 a.m. to
3:00 p.m. at the University of California, Irvine. He noted that attendance is free and includes
lunch and free parking.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 5 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.
City Council Minutes  2  March 13, 2018
 Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of February 27, 2018, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated February 16, 2018 in the Amount of $1,234,820.44

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated February 23, 2018 in the Amount of $2,750,518.27

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Semi-Annual Financial Report for the Community Development Financing Authority
  - For the Six Months Ended December 31, 2017

  Received and filed.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

5.  Marguerite Parkway Corridor Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (CIP 17230)

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented a brief overview of the signal
  synchronization project. He noted that it is 80% grant-funded with a 20% City match that
  is typically made up of gas tax or Measure M funds.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  authorize the Director of Public Works to submit a request to the Orange County
  Transportation Authority to extend the expenditure deadline for Measure M2 grant funds
  in the amount of $48,960 to Fiscal Year 2019-2020 for the Ongoing Maintenance and
  Monitoring Phase of the Marguerite Parkway Traffic Signal Synchronization Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  3  March 13, 2018
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

6.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Chief Rob Capobianco presented an update on OCFA activity including an outline of call
  responses, a Community Emergency Preparedness Academy within the Casta del Sol
  community, water rescue training and a structure fire on Obrero Drive.

  Mayor Sachs presented the OCFA Board Meeting report.

7.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Sachs announced that he had no report at this time.

8.  Establish Voting Rights Ad Hoc Committee

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: questioned the City's process and said that the City is in legal
  jeopardy and creating an ad hoc committee is a stall tactic to avoid going to district voting
  in 2018.

  Mayor Sachs appointed Mayor Pro Tem Raths and Council Member Kelley to the Voting
  Rights Ad Hoc Committee.

STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

9.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum reiterated that the City Council has been assessing the voting rights
situation and the attorney from Shenkman and Hughes now indicates that he is pulling back on his
threat of a lawsuit. She said she doesn't understand how that could not be clear to the public but if
anyone is confused, please reach out to the City Council for clarification. She also noted that the
City Council regularly forms ad hoc committees which involve many people who come together
to study a topic and bring recommendations back to the Council to be vetted and to allow for public
comments. Council Member Bucknum said that it was an amazing sight over the weekend when
the three pools at the Marguerite Aquatics Center were filled with water in 48 hours. She said the
City embarked upon the renovation of the aquatics center when it was about 10 years overdue and
this valuable City asset will re-open on April 7, 2018, at 10:00 a.m. Residents can park at Trabuco
City Council Minutes  4  March 13, 2018
 Hills High School and take the free shuttle to the grand opening event or ride their bikes or walk
if they live nearby. Council Member Bucknum discussed additional events including South Orange
County Senior Day which will be hosted by Senator Bates and Assemblyman Brough on Friday,
March 16 at the Murray Community Center and the City’s Irish Fest on the Village Green from
11:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. on St. Patrick’s Day.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell mentioned an email he saw from a very grateful Marine who was rescued
by Orange County Fire Authority personnel when his convoy vehicle was stuck on the side of the
freeway. Council Member Goodell outlined his attendance at an Association of California Cities
Legislative Advocacy meeting where he and Council Member Bucknum met with Senators and
Assembly Members, as well as the Director of CalPERS and the Secretary of Transportation. He
said they were enlightened on issues facing the state and new legislation concerning affordable
housing, homelessness and other relevant topics. He noted that these are valuable meetings because
the Council Members get to talk face-to-face with state representatives and everyone gets a better
understanding of the issues. He also discussed his attendance at a Pension Reform Workshop last
week which provided beneficial information on the crisis and impending doom with the California
retirement system, and yesterday’s groundbreaking ceremony for the new stadium at Saddleback
College which, he said, is a very exciting project.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she just returned from a visit with her grandchildren in
Indiana so she missed a few recent events. She did however attend a forum on February 21 called
“Let’s Talk Cannabis” which was hosted by Assemblyman Brough and Senator Bates. She said it
was a very informative program and was well attended. Council Member Kelley thanked the
student speaker from the Community of Character Committee who did a great job talking about
the character word of the month during public comments earlier in the meeting. She noted that the
Character Committee is comprised of about 20 high school students and 8 adults who plan
activities and work at many of the City’s events. Council Member Kelley said that the character
materials are distributed at all 25 Mission Viejo schools and she closed her comments with quotes
about this month’s character word, integrity.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce monthly mixer
will be held in unison with the grand opening of the Volvo auto dealership from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m.
on March 15. He also noted that the Mission Viejo Rotary Club’s annual Texas Hold 'Em
fundraiser is on April 14, 2018, with check-in at 4:00 p.m., dinner at 5:00 p.m. and card games
beginning at 6:00 p.m. Mayor Pro Tem Raths said he looks forward to the ad hoc committee update
on the civic core area which will come to the Council in April. He said he is curious to see how
the City is progressing on cleanup of the Village Center area. He also asked the City Manager to
task staff with looking at the parking issues on Via Fabricante and Obrero where auto repair shops
are putting cars on the streets. He said it appears there is not enough parking and signage in the
area is getting out of control. The business owners have gotten together to try and find some
solutions and he would like the City’s involvement. Mayor Pro Tem Raths reminded residents that
City Council Minutes  5  March 13, 2018
 the Easter Bunny is live at the Shops at Mission Viejo and he thanked Lieutenant Vuong for the
quick response on social media to assure residents that the Sheriff’s Department is conducting
extra patrols in areas where break-ins have been occurring.

Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs announced that he had no comments this evening.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:26 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, March 27, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

_____________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 27, 2018

City Council Minutes  6  March 13, 2018
